How I Set Up Filter Media for Clearer Aquarium Water! There are several ways to set up aquarium filter media, and the arrangement you choose can affect water clarity, cleaning, and maintenance. Over the last year, I have tested different setups, and this layered approach has worked best for me personally. The water flows from bottom to top in this example, passing through progressively finer mechanical filtration before reaching the biological media. I start with 30 PPI foam, follow it with 50 PPI foam, and then add a backup layer of filter floss to catch smaller particles that make it through the sponges. PPI means pores per inch, with the higher number indicating a finer foam. This coarse-to-fine arrangement helps spread the mechanical filtration across several layers instead of asking the finest material to catch everything. After that comes the biological media, which provides surfaces for the bacteria involved in the aquarium nitrogen cycle. More 30 PPI foam works here, although ceramics, sintered glass, pumice, or lava rock are other options. Foam can provide both mechanical and biological filtration, so you don’t need expensive media for every filter setup. You can also include chemical filtration after these stages if you have a reason to use it, but I usually leave it out of my tanks. A simple block of filter foam still works perfectly well, and my basic setups have maintained the biological cycle without issue. The main difference I have noticed is that they allow more particles to remain in the water column. Another option I have been testing uses affordable foam in different grades, without a dedicated layer of biological media. This offers a useful middle ground between cost, water clarity, and easy cleaning, with the option of adding filter floss for extra polishing. Always check which direction water travels through your filter before arranging the layers. For my planted tanks, the aim is reliable filtration, clearer water, and a setup that stays affordable and straightforward to maintain. #aquarium  #fishtank  #fishkeeping
